new_entities.name: TAVI for severe aortic stenosis in low-risk patients
aliases: transcatheter aortic valve replacement in low-risk severe aortic stenosis
new_entities.description: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation or replacement for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis in patients at low surgical risk.

edges.effect_quant: Low-risk randomized-trial meta-analysis found lower overall mortality with TAVI than surgery (RR 0.61). PARTNER 3 showed a lower 1-year composite event rate including death, stroke, or rehospitalization (HR 0.54), while Evolut Low Risk showed noninferiority for death or disabling stroke at 24 months.
edges.population: adults with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis who are candidates for valve replacement and have low predicted surgical risk
edges.mechanism: Less invasive transcatheter treatment may reduce perioperative physiologic stress, bleeding, kidney injury, and postoperative atrial fibrillation, which can translate into lower early mortality in selected low-risk populations.
edges.summary: The low-risk TAVI story is no longer only about noninferiority. Contemporary trial synthesis supports at least an early mortality advantage, although the magnitude is modest and longer-term durability questions remain important.
edges.caveats: A large part of the signal is driven by early follow-up, whereas longer-term survival differences narrow and may evolve over time. Device durability, pacemaker need, and paravalvular leak remain relevant tradeoffs, especially in younger low-risk patients.

evidence.citation: Hofer F et al 2020 Clin Res Cardiol
evidence.notes: Transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in low-risk patients: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
